messages:
Maria (support): FYI: ACME (dedicated) reporting sustained 503s + 10-20s tail latency. They say traffic spike but autoscaler isnt bringing replicas up fast enough. min_replicas=2, traffic needs ~12. Can someone triage?
Jamal (eng-runtime): :eyes: Can you paste the exact request pattern and any error payloads? Is it 429s or upstream 503s?
Maria (support): Mostly 503 upstream from our gateway. Customer sent these quick repro steps: 
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/dedicated/acme/infer -d '{"input":"<long prompt>"}'
2) Send 120 concurrent requests over 30s
They also gave this single request response: 
{
  "status":503,
  "error":"service_unavailable",
  "detail":"no healthy endpoints for model: rdx-3.1-dedicated-acme"
}
Priya (eng-platform): Can you run `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-acme` and check the controller events? Also check the autoscaler logs for backoff.
Maria (support): Pasted output from customer (sanitized):
```
NAMESPACE            NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
dedicated-acme       rdx-svc-0                            0/1     Pending   0          2m
dedicated-acme       rdx-svc-1                            0/1     Pending   0          2m
dedicated-acme       rdx-svc-2                            0/1     Pending   0          2m
```
And events: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x3 over 2m)  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 2 InsufficientGPU, 8 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
Normal   NotTriggerScaleUp 2m              cluster-autoscaler  pod didn't trigger scale-up: may be re-queued
Warning  FailedCreatePod   1m              kubelet             failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create containerd task: failed to reserve device resources
```
Jamal (eng-runtime): Key lines: InsufficientGPU + reserve device failure. Could be quota or the nodepool couldnt get GPU instance because of cloud quota or billing blocker. Any cloud error logs?
Ben (eng-infra): I pulled the cluster events via our backend for acme-dedicated: there are repeated GCE API errors: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Quota 'NVIDIA_TESLA_V100' exceeded in region us-west1`. Also saw `403: Billing account disabled` for one of the node creation attempts.
Maria (support): Wait, customer just said their billing is fine. Could that be our org-level billing?
Alex (customer-success): I checked the customer's account page — billing is active, no invoices overdue. However, their dedicated deployment sits under our partner cloud project in us-west1; partner account shows quota at limit. Reached out to partner ops.
Priya (eng-platform): That explains why pods are Pending: autoscaler asks for nodes, cloud rejects due to quota/billing so we backoff. Our autoscaler logic treats repeated node creation failures as transient and applies exponential backoff: 
```
scale_controller: backoff=2s,next_delay=8s,fail_count=3
```
After N failures it marks the rollout as degraded and stops creating more attempts for that burst. That causes the slow ramp and 503s.
Jamal (eng-runtime): Two actionable workstreams: (1) short-term: adjust fallback policy so we can serve on smaller model variant or CPU-only nodes; (2) infra: surface the cloud quota/billing rejection as a customer-facing incident so CS can coordinate with partner.
Ben (eng-infra): Right. We can also relax the autoscaler backoff threshold for customer-tier=enterprise so bursts retry faster (but careful with noisy neighbor impact).
Maria (support): Customer wants timeline — they reported impact started ~2005004200. Any quick mitigation I can offer them?
Priya (eng-platform): Offer a temporary manual scale (if you have reserved capacity) or enable fallback model route that swaps to rdx-3.0-small (CPU fallback) for this customer. I can flip a routing flag for acme for the next 30 minutes.
Alex (customer-success): Do it please, we need to stop errors. Also opening a ticket with partner ops for quota request.
OpsBot: Created incident ticket INC-2038 and pager on-call eng-infra.
Jamal (eng-runtime): For long term: we should add a preflight check during scale-up that queries cloud response codes and surfaces a mapped human-readable reason: quota vs billing vs capacity. Then autoscaler can decide to trigger fallback routing immediately instead of backing off.
Ben (eng-infra): Agreed. I'll draft a PR to: increase log visibility, add `cloud_error_type` tag (QUOTA|BILLING|CAPACITY), and lower backoff multiplier for enterprise tenants.
Priya (eng-platform): Also add an alert: "provisioning_failure_rate > 5% in 5m" that creates a support ticket automatically.
Maria (support): Done: told customer we enabled CPU fallback and are coordinating with partner ops. They confirmed reduced errors but slightly higher latency. :thumbsup:
Alex (customer-success): Noted. Keeping ACME as high priority until partner confirms quota increase or we free capacity.
Jamal (eng-runtime): Follow-up items:
- Ben: PR for logging + backoff tweak (ETA 2d)
- Priya: temporary routing flip + alert (ETA 30m)
- Ben/Priya: investigate partner billing flags (sync w/ Alex)
- Maria: gather exact timestamps for spike and request traces (so we can measure ramp time)
Maria (support): I'll attach traces to the incident. Thanks team.
Ben (eng-infra): :white_check_mark: starting PR branch `infra/sku-quota-visibility`.
OpsBot: Incident INC-2038 updated: severity=P2, assignees=[Ben, Priya, Jamal].
